title: Industry Pulse — AI / Agent Ecosystem

bullets.title: Anthropic prices its IPO at $83/share (Nov 18) and starts trading on Nasdaq as ANT today (Nov 19)
bullets.summary: Anthropic priced above its $70-$78 range, raising about $81.3B gross on roughly 980M shares (Renaissance Capital figures); reported valuation is about $1.38T-$1.5T fully diluted, and the debut drew a coalition 'MisAnthropic Statement' critique of its safety branding.
bullets.how: The Construct: the core vendor is now public, so expect quarterly pressure on pricing, rate limits and packaging; keep the model-neutral fallback routes tested. PRAGMA: a credibility point when pitching Claude-based operator stacks to clients. Brand 9 Signs: no direct effect.

bullets.title: Claude Code v2.1.327-v2.1.328: 'claude mcp add-json' reads config from stdin, and mcp_tool hooks can set onFailure: block
bullets.summary: The two releases (Nov 16-19) let a script register an MCP server by piping JSON, and let a hook that calls an MCP tool stop the action when the check fails instead of just warning.
bullets.how: The Construct: script MCP server setup for every Hermes worker from one JSON source, and turn the important guard hooks (spend, publish, send) into blocking gates. PRAGMA: a concrete 'hard gate' pattern for client deployments. Brand 9 Signs: block site deploys or order placements when a check fails.

bullets.title: Citi, PNC and Citizens change their terms (Nov 18): customers are liable for what their AI agents do, even after a hack
bullets.summary: The banks updated account terms so that activity by third-party AI agents acting for a customer is the customer's responsibility, including if the agent or its credentials are compromised.
bullets.how: The Construct and Brand 9 Signs: any agent that touches bank, card or vendor accounts (Signs365 orders, Stripe) needs a scoped credential, a hard spend cap and a log, because the loss lands on the business. PRAGMA: a strong governance talking point for clients.

bullets.title: Anthropic linked billing beta (Nov 17): third-party apps bill Claude usage to the customer's own org with spend caps
bullets.summary: Customers link their Claude org so third-party platforms (19 at launch, including Linear, Ramp, Railway, Asana and ClickHouse) bill usage to it without an API key; a billing_policy field picks who pays, and monthly or per-app limits are set in Console.
bullets.how: The Construct: put each tool that calls Claude on its own capped line. PRAGMA: ship client tools where the client pays Anthropic directly and PRAGMA never holds their key. Brand 9 Signs: indirect.

bullets.title: Google ships Gemini 4 Neon (Nov 18): $3/$15 per 1M tokens, 1M context, claims #1 on the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index
bullets.summary: Google's new model has four thinking levels and a 1M-token context and claims 58.6 on the Coding Agent Index; it lands a day after OpenAI's GPT-6.2 Astra ($8/$40) and Sol ($2/$10).
bullets.how: The Construct: run one standing task (a Pulse scan or a site-fix recipe) on Neon and Sol against Claude to compare cost and quality before moving any route. PRAGMA: keep the pitch model-neutral. Brand 9 Signs: no direct effect.

praxis_lesson: Liability for agent actions now sits with the operator (banks just made that explicit), so every Construct agent that can spend or send must pass a blocking gate, use a scoped credential and stay under a cap it cannot raise; Claude Code's new onFailure: block hooks make that gate cheap to build.
